findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Quantify and record the observed root-disk fill rate (GiB/hour or %/hour derived from the incident series or a du delta) so AC4's plateau simulation has a concrete input.
evidence: AC4: 'a test or simulation driving the documented fill rate and showing usage plateaus below the bound'
Recovery: 'At the observed fill rate the larger disk postpones recurrence' — rate referenced but not stated numerically
Observed series shows percent values only, no byte/time growth figure
findings.finding: AC4's proving simulation depends on a 'documented fill rate' that the plan never quantifies — the incident data gives disk-used PERCENTAGES (90–94%) over 30-min buckets, not a GiB/hour fill rate.
scenarios: Executor builds the ceiling mechanism but cannot parameterize or run the plateau simulation because no fill rate is on record
findings.suggested_fix: Add the measured fill rate (e.g. derived from AC3's du breakdown and the 29 GiB working set) to the plan and reference that number in AC4.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add/clarify an acceptance criterion that explicitly sets the EvaluationPeriods / datapoints-to-alarm so the alarm fires on a single (or short-run) breaching datapoint, reconciling AC2's single-datapoint expectation with the current EvaluationPeriods=3.
evidence: Defect 2: 'because the disk was breaching but had not yet accumulated 3 breaching periods'
AC1 changes only 'TreatMissingData becomes breaching (or missing)'
AC2 requires 'an alarm exists that would have fired on the 2026-09-01T23:33 94% datapoint' — a single datapoint, incompatible with EvaluationPeriods=3
findings.finding: Defect 2 names EvaluationPeriods=3 as a co-cause (the alarm 'had not yet accumulated 3 breaching periods'), but no acceptance criterion explicitly requires changing EvaluationPeriods / datapoints-to-alarm; AC1 only flips TreatMissingData, and AC2 states an outcome (fire on the single 23:33 94% datapoint) that is unreachable with EvaluationPeriods=3 unless that setting is also changed.
scenarios: Executor flips TreatMissingData only, leaves EvaluationPeriods=3; the replay in AC2 still does not fire on the single 94% datapoint and the diagnosed 3-period lag persists
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AC1 (or add AC1b) to specify the new EvaluationPeriods/datapoints-to-alarm value and verify it via describe-alarms alongside the TreatMissingData change.

findings.checklist_item: Correct the alarm description to note the live config is 2-of-3 (evaluation_periods=3, datapoints_to_alarm=2), and have AC2 name datapoints_to_alarm as part of the threshold/period configuration being replayed/changed.
evidence: monitoring_autodeploy.tf:224-225 'evaluation_periods = 3' AND 'datapoints_to_alarm = 2'
Plan states only '**EvaluationPeriods = 3**' with no mention of datapoints_to_alarm

AC2 requires 'an alarm exists that would have fired on the 2026-09-01T23:33 94% datapoint ... replaying the recorded series against the new threshold/period configuration' — the datapoints_to_alarm field is part of that configuration

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile AC1 with the existing S7 `rebar-gerrit-gate-down` dead-man's-switch: state whether the disk alarm should page on missing-data at all (given gate-down already does), and if so justify the double-page — or instead target firing LATENCY so the disk alarm trips while the host is still alive.
evidence: Live: monitoring_autodeploy.tf L229-231 `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"` with comment: 'A dead probe/host is caught by the S7 gate-down alarm (treat_missing_data = breaching there); duplicating that here would double-page on host loss.'
monitoring.tf L61-86: `rebar-gerrit-gate-down` already has `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` and is the intended host/probe-dead alarm
Plan Defect 2 concedes 'The only thing that fired was rebar-gerrit-gate-down ... at 02:05' — i.e. the dead-man's-switch exists and fired
Plan gives no rationale for accepting the double-page or for why the disk alarm (not gate-down) should be the host-death signal
findings.finding: AC1's chosen mechanism (flip TreatMissingData to `breaching` on both disk alarms) reverts a deliberate anti-double-page design and duplicates the dead-man's-switch the S7 gate-down alarm already provides, without stating why the double-page is now acceptable.
scenarios: Any future host-loss event now pages twice (gate-down + both disk alarms flipping to ALARM on missing data)
Operators who tuned out redundant disk-alarm host-loss pages could miss the distinct disk-fill-while-alive signal
findings.suggested_fix: Frame the fix as 'the disk-pressure condition must alert before host death' and choose between (a) tightening the threshold/period so it fires on live datapoints (see AC2), and (b) making missing-data breaching; if (b), explicitly acknowledge and accept the double-page with gate-down, or dedupe via a composite alarm.

findings.checklist_item: Correct the alarm description to the live 2-of-3 form (evaluation_periods=3, datapoints_to_alarm=2) and re-derive why it did not fire on the recorded >85 samples before selecting AC2's threshold/period change.
evidence: Plan: 'EvaluationPeriods = 3' and 'the disk was breaching but had not yet accumulated 3 breaching periods'
Live: monitoring_autodeploy.tf L224-226 `evaluation_periods = 3`, `datapoints_to_alarm = 2`, `threshold = 85`, comparison GreaterThanThreshold — a 2-of-3 M-of-N alarm, not 'needs 3 consecutive'
Observed series 92/94/92/91/92/90 are all >85, which a 2-of-3 threshold alarm would satisfy — so 'not yet 3 breaching' does not explain the non-fire
findings.finding: The Defect-2 root-cause narrative and AC2 mis-describe the live alarm as requiring 3 breaching periods (EvaluationPeriods=3), omitting `datapoints_to_alarm=2`; the 2-of-3 threshold semantics contradict the plan's stated reason the alarm never fired.
scenarios: AC2 replay is designed against a mischaracterized period model and validates the wrong parameter change
The true cause (e.g. 30-min-max sampling vs 5-min period, or metric-latency vs missing-data OK transition) is left un-diagnosed

scenarios: Implementer re-implements an acute-prune tier that already exists, duplicating 3cef
Implementer picks a ceiling mechanism (e.g. quota/cgroup, image GC daemon, LVM thin-pool cap) with no stated fitness rationale and it is rejected in review

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the AC1/AC2 alarm changes land in the Terraform source (monitoring_autodeploy.tf / monitoring.tf) via plan-before-apply, and update the inline `notBreaching` rationale comments, so the fix is durable and does not drift/revert on the next apply.
evidence: AC1: "Verified by `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms` showing the new setting" — verification is against live state, not the IaC source.
monitoring_autodeploy.tf:231 `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"` with rationale at lines 229-231 is IaC-managed; a live-only edit drifts.
monitoring.tf:237 gerrit_data_disk_high also sets `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"` in Terraform.
findings.finding: AC1/AC2 change the treat_missing_data / threshold-period configuration of alarms that are already Terraform-managed (monitoring_autodeploy.tf root_disk_pressure; monitoring.tf gerrit_data_disk_high), but the plan specifies the change and its verification only in terms of the live AWS state (`aws cloudwatch describe-alarms`, induced publish-stop) and does not state the change must land in the Terraform source with a plan-before-apply. An out-of-band console/CLI edit to satisfy the ACs would drift from the committed IaC, and the next `terraform apply` would revert treat_missing_data to the documented deliberate `notBreaching` (monitoring_autodeploy.tf:229-231).
scenarios: Operator changes the setting via console to pass AC1; a later routine `terraform apply` (or autodeploy) reverts it and silently restores the dead-man's-switch inversion.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC1/AC2 that the change is made in the Terraform resources (root_disk_pressure, gerrit_data_disk_high), the existing notBreaching rationale comments are corrected, and verification includes a clean `terraform plan` (no residual diff) in addition to `describe-alarms`.

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile AC1's treat_missing_data change with the documented deliberate notBreaching choice (monitoring_autodeploy.tf:229-231) and the existing gate-down host-down backstop: state why the S7 breaching alarm is insufficient, or scope AC1/AC2 to threshold/evaluation-period tuning that would have fired on the 23:33 datapoint without duplicating host-loss paging.
